title: Enhancing Electron Microscopy Image Classification Using Data Augmentation
problem: Manual labeling for machine learning is tedious and labor-intensive, resulting in scarce scientific datasets suitable for deep learning. Understanding how combining multiple data augmentation methods sequentially affects classification performance on small datasets remains largely unexplored.
motivation: Data augmentation can extend limited scientific datasets for deep learning, but its effectiveness and optimal combination strategies are not well understood.
method: The study generates single, double, and quadruple-augmented datasets for electron microscopy image classification using six standard augmentation methods. Classification accuracy is evaluated on three CNN architectures (DenseNet169, MobileNetV2, ResNet101V2) using binary classification tasks. The impact of augmentation order and number of simultaneous methods are systematically analyzed.
key_novelty: Discovery of a non-monotonic relationship between the number of simultaneous augmentation methods and classification accuracy, demonstrating that order of application significantly affects performance (up to 2.6% difference).
contributions: Empirical investigation of combined data augmentation effects on limited microscopy datasets
Identification of non-monotonic performance trade-off between augmentation count and accuracy
Finding that augmentation method order significantly impacts binary classification performance
Evidence that optimal augmentation strategies are domain and use-case specific

metrics.accuracy: binary classification accuracy improvements with up to 2.6% difference based on augmentation order

limitations: Evaluation limited to electron microscopy domain; generalizability to other scientific imaging tasks not discussed.
primary_theme: Data augmentation optimization for small image datasets
